newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PRISONERS VOTE DESPITE CANDIDATES' SNUB.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PRISONERS VOTE DESPITE CANDIDATES' SNUB.

text.p: Czech prisoners, determined to exercise their democratic rights, voted for Senate elections in their jail on Friday despite being snubbed by every candidate.
"Our prisoners still feel somewhat offended by the fact that all the candidates completely forgot about them during the campaign," said Jiri Meznik, governor of Kurim jail.
Meznik told the Czech news agency CTK that not a single leaflet had been sent to the jail near the second city of Brno.
But the snub does not seem to have dampened the enthusiasm of the 760 convicts and remand prisoners, captive voters though they may be.

Meznik said that half of them voted in the first round last week, far above the national average of 35 percent, and he forecast turnout would be about the same again in the second round run-off on Friday and Saturday.

Meznik said preferences among the prisoners ranged from the pro-business Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus to those who reckon "it was better under the communists", who were overthrown in 1989, CTK said.
